finding: Minotaur levels run a hidden pursuit clock (150 s, or 210 s on listed depths): a one-in-five warning at arrival minus 30 s summons a nine-human brigade, then the boss arrives at the start point with a hint and sting. Summon traps (interval, count, cycles, fail percent), sleepers (gnome 1 in 8, imp 1 in 4, tick durations) and mimics (inert until touched) round it out. Defects: the brigade leader id is declared inside the loop so no follower links form; the warning is a single-tick roll with no retry. Idea adapted with a one-second window and a three-attacker cap. Level counts are in the data pack, which is not in the box; code read in full, data not read.

Spawn points with a respawn plus or minus variance, weighted entries filtered by time window, condition and per-type cap, a grace despawn for unengaged creatures, a random-step roambox with a random pause, a 10-grid-type wander set, an idle-zone freeze, and a timed lair gate through spawn-condition events. Three defects: random pause falls back to 14 s when min equals max; variance floor applied after the roll; despawn modes 3 and 4 return before the point timer (end-to-end not traced). Shape only under GPL-3.0. Zone spawn rows and client are not in the box, so walk density is not countable and the server half is the only half read. AU018 wrongly says no server source is present.
